commentary: The EvidencePack Collection Scope establishes a high-sensitivity evidence program for Incident ABC, focused on comprehensive collection, strict chain-of-custody, and readiness for internal and legal review. It designates stakeholders (Requestor, Evidence Custodian, Legal) and enforces role-based access with multi-factor authentication and encryption in transit and at rest. The scope covers a wide range of sources—such as forensic disk images, memory dumps, logs, email archives, cloud artifacts, mobile backups, configuration files, and database exports—while mandating that collection not alter evidence and minimize business disruption. Retention is set to seven years with secure deletion via overwrite and cryptographic erase, and deliverables include an EvidencePack Archive (with hash manifest and custody logs) and an Acquisition Report. Acceptance requires that all listed evidence types are present, cryptographic hashes and custody records accompany each item, and Legal approves any cross-border transfers.

artifacts.expert_comment:
The EvidencePack Collection Scope defines an operating model centered on comprehensive collection, strict chain-of-custody, and readiness for internal and legal review. It designates stakeholders (Requestor, Evidence Custodian, Legal) and enforces a High-sensitivity regime with role-based access, approved users, multi-factor authentication, and encryption in transit and at rest. The scope covers disk images (forensic), memory dumps, log files, email archives, cloud service artifacts, mobile device backups, configuration files, and database exports. This foundation supports collecting and preserving all relevant digital evidence for Incident ABC while tightly governing access.

Execution is shaped by clear constraints: no evidence may be altered during acquisition, collection must minimize disruption, and cross-jurisdictional transfers require Legal sign-off. Acceptance criteria raise the bar on auditability by requiring that all listed evidence types are present, cryptographic hashes accompany each item, and chain-of-custody records are maintained, with Legal approval for any cross-border transfers. Retention is set to seven years, with secure deletion via overwrite and cryptographic erase, extending control through end-of-life. These elements collectively build a defensible, lifecycle-based posture.

For decision-makers, align governance, access control, and operational plans to the named gates: objectives, constraints, evidence types, acceptance criteria, and deliverables. Ensure role assignments and controls are implemented as specified, and that deliverables consistently include an EvidencePack Archive with a SHA-256 hash manifest and chain-of-custody logs, plus an Acquisition Report. Plan for encrypted storage and authorized access over the seven-year retention period, and obtain Legal sign-off where data must cross jurisdictions. Build collection workflows that demonstrate non-alteration and minimize disruption, as both are required at acquisition.

The EvidencePack Collection Scope for Incident ABC establishes a high-sensitivity evidence program centered on comprehensive collection, strict chain-of-custody, and readiness for internal and legal review. It names stakeholders and enforces role-based access with multi-factor authentication and encryption in transit and at rest, while defining explicit evidence types, constraints, retention, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

What this means for decision-makers:

- Governance and access controls:
  - Stakeholders: Requestor, Evidence Custodian, Legal
  - High sensitivity classification with role-based access, approved users, multi-factor required, encryption at rest and in transit

- Evidence coverage to anticipate and request:
  - Forensic disk images, memory dumps, log files, email archives
  - Cloud service artifacts, mobile device backups, configuration files, database exports

- Collection constraints to uphold operational integrity:
  - No evidence may be altered during acquisition
  - Collection must minimize business disruption
  - Cross-jurisdictional transfers require Legal sign-off

- Retention and disposal expectations:
  - Retention period: seven years
  - Secure deletion: overwrite and cryptographic erase

- Deliverables and acceptance criteria for legal and internal readiness:
  - EvidencePack Archive with a SHA-256 hash manifest and chain-of-custody logs
  - Acquisition Report documenting the collection
  - Acceptance requires all listed evidence types, cryptographic hashes and custody records for each item, and Legal approval for any cross-border transfers

Net result: a clear, enforceable scope that aligns people, process, and artifacts for Incident ABC, ensuring comprehensive collection, protected access, and evidentiary integrity from acquisition through retention and secure deletion.
